Week one of the voyage is in the books, and I’m learning that “seasick” comes in at least five different flavors. The first two days I could barely look at the ocean, let alone eat. Then, somewhere around day three, my stomach just gave up complaining and I was back to normal. We’ve been sailing south through some pretty rough water, and everything on board is strapped down — chairs, laptops, even the coffee machine. The science team has already started setting up for their first sampling station, which means we’ll be up at odd hours dragging heavy gear on deck. Tomorrow we cross into colder water, and I’m told we might see our first iceberg. I’ll keep you posted, assuming my fingers don’t freeze.
